```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
library(flextable)

d <- readRDS("report_data.rds")

# One table style for the whole document. layout = "autofit" with width = 1 makes the
# table fill the text block and stay a real Word table -- resizable, editable, and
# selectable cell by cell -- rather than a picture of one.
# A grouped_data (flextable::as_grouped_data) gets its group labels as spanning rows.
# `header` reshapes the header (extra rows, merges) BEFORE the styling, so the styling
# reaches every header row.
ft <- function(x, size = 9.5, header = identity) {
  (if (inherits(x, "grouped_data")) as_flextable(x, hide_grouplabel = TRUE) else flextable(x)) |>
    header() |>
    theme_booktabs() |>
    font(fontname = "Calibri", part = "all") |>
    fontsize(size = size, part = "all") |>
    bold(part = "header") |>
    align(align = "center", part = "all") |>
    align(j = 1, align = "left", part = "all") |>
    valign(valign = "bottom", part = "header") |>
    padding(padding.top = 2.5, padding.bottom = 2.5, part = "all") |>
    set_table_properties(layout = "autofit", width = 1)
}

counts <- function(x, j) colformat_num(x, j = j, big.mark = ",", digits = 0)
one_dp <- function(x, j) colformat_double(x, j = j, digits = 1)
two_dp <- function(x, j) colformat_double(x, j = j, digits = 2)

rule       <- fp_border_default(color = "grey45", width = 1)
group_rule <- fp_border_default(color = "grey65", width = 1)

# Every NNT table is the same shape, so it takes the same treatment: two header rows,
# the stage on top spanning its columns, with the single columns merged down through
# both; counts with thousands separators (the stage cells arrive as formatted text and
# need none); and rules marking off the blocks. MCI and dementia come first, then any
# CI and the early catches, with a heavier rule between the two pairs. The PCP tables have no early-catch block (see 01_paper2_tables.R).
nnt_ft <- function(x) {
  early <- any(startsWith(names(x), "Coincidentally detected before onset"))
  ratio <- "Tests per 10 detected"
  top <- c("Strategy", "Tests completed", "Mean tests per person ever tested",
           "MCI at time of positive test", "Dementia at time of positive test",
           "Any CI at time of positive test",
           if (early) "Healthy at time of positive test")
  sub <- c("", "", "", "n (%)", ratio, "n (%)", ratio,
           "n (%)", ratio, "Time from onset to detection, mean (SD)",
           if (early) c("n (%)", "Time from detection to onset, mean (SD)"))
  header <- function(f) {
    f <- f |>
      set_header_labels(values = setNames(as.list(sub), names(x))) |>
      add_header_row(values = top, colwidths = c(1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, if (early) 2))
    for (j in 1:3) f <- merge_at(f, i = 1:2, j = j, part = "header")
    f
  }
  ft(x, header = header) |>
    counts(j = "Tests administered") |>
    two_dp(j = "Tests per person tested") |>
    hline(i = 1, j = 4:ncol(x), border = group_rule, part = "header") |>
    vline(j = intersect(c(3, 5, 10), seq_len(ncol(x) - 1)), border = group_rule, part = "all") |>
    vline(j = 7, border = rule, part = "all")
}

# The results tables stack two blocks of the same strategies, first cycle then program
# end. Two header rows, "Sensitivity" spanning its three columns and the single columns
# merged down through both; the Time label merged down its block, with the rule between
# the blocks. Superscripts 1-3 point at the numbered notes under each table.
start_age    <- min(d$testing_window)
program_yrs  <- d$end_age - start_age
# Built as text: as_paragraph() would print a bare number as "80.0".
time_labels  <- list(
  as_paragraph("First cycle in which a test is offered", as_sup("1"),
               paste0("\n(cohort aged ", start_age, ")")),
  as_paragraph(paste0("By year ", program_yrs, " (end of program,\ncohort aged ", d$end_age, ")")))
time_short   <- c(`First Cycle` = "First cycle", `By Program End` = paste("By year", program_yrs))

results_ft <- function(x) {
  n <- nrow(x) %/% 2
  top <- c("Time", "Strategy", "Eligible tested", "Sensitivity",
           "Specificity", "PPV", "NPV", "Accuracy")
  header <- function(f) {
    f <- f |>
      set_header_labels(Sensitivity = "Any CI", `Sensitivity, MCI` = "MCI",
                        `Sensitivity, dementia` = "Dementia") |>
      add_header_row(values = top, colwidths = c(1, 1, 1, 3, 1, 1, 1, 1))
    for (j in c(1:3, 7:10)) f <- merge_at(f, i = 1:2, j = j, part = "header")
    f |>
      compose(i = 1, j = 3, part = "header",
              value = as_paragraph("Eligible tested", as_sup("2"), ",\nn (%)")) |>
      compose(i = 2, j = 6, part = "header", value = as_paragraph("Dementia", as_sup("3")))
  }
  ft(x, header = header) |>
    hline(i = 1, j = 4:6, border = group_rule, part = "header") |>
    compose(i = 1,     j = 1, value = time_labels[[1]]) |>
    compose(i = n + 1, j = 1, value = time_labels[[2]]) |>
    merge_at(i = 1:n, j = 1) |>
    merge_at(i = (n + 1):(2 * n), j = 1) |>
    valign(j = 1, valign = "center", part = "body") |>
    hline(i = n, border = rule)
}

# The tables carry point estimates only; the dementia-sensitivity intervals, carried on
# the table as an attribute, are spelled out in its note 3 instead.
sens_dem_note <- function(x) {
  ci <- attr(x, "sens_dem_ci")
  by_time <- vapply(unique(ci$Time), function(tm) {
    r <- ci[ci$Time == tm, ]
    paste0("*", time_short[[tm]], "*: ", paste(r$Strategy, r$sens_dem_ci, collapse = "; "), ".")
  }, character(1))
  paste("^3^ 95% Wilson intervals for dementia sensitivity.", paste(by_time, collapse = " "),
        "Intervals reflect Monte Carlo error only; because the strategies share random",
        "numbers, differences between them are more precise than overlapping intervals suggest.")
}
```

Cohort of `r format(d$n_ind, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)` individuals, simulated
from age 50. Testing window ages `r min(d$testing_window)`--`r max(d$testing_window)`;
program end reported at age `r d$end_age`. All figures and tables are drawn from
simulation run `r d$run_id`.

# 1. Main text

## Figure 1. Share of the starting cohort in each outcome, by strategy and age

![](figures/counts_and_shares.png){width=9.2in}

\newpage

## Table 1. Program performance, by strategy

```{r tab1}
results_ft(d$results_main)
```

All values other than counts are percentages and describe the program, not the test:
eligible people who were never tested count as misses (false negatives or true negatives).
The second block is the cumulative snapshot at age `r d$end_age`. CI, cognitive
impairment; MCI, mild cognitive impairment; PPV, positive predictive value; NPV, negative
predictive value.

^1^ Read at each person's own first cycle due for a test.

^2^ The number tested and their share of those eligible: of those due a test that cycle in
the first block; of everyone ever eligible during the program in the second.

`r sens_dem_note(d$results_main)`

\newpage

## Figure 2. Annual program performance, by strategy and age

![](figures/annual_performance.png){width=9.2in}

(A) Of the impaired people in the program not yet detected at the start of the year
(including those newly impaired that year), the share the program detects that year;
eligible people who were never tested count as not detected, as in Table 1. The solid line
counts a person who already held a positive result and became impaired that year as
detected, as Table 1 does; the dashed line counts only positive tests given that year.
(B) Of the people given their first positive result that year, the share impaired at the
time. The inclusive strategy tests a third of its cohort each year, so everyone is first
offered a test by age 67; its curves rise over those years as the first round completes.

\newpage

## Table 2. Number needed to test, by strategy

```{r tab2}
nnt_ft(d$nnt_main)
```

*Tests completed* counts every BHA from age `r min(d$testing_window)` to
`r max(d$testing_window)`, and is the numerator of every ratio in the table: no test can
be aimed at one stage alone, so the stage-specific ratios do not average to the overall
one. *Mean tests per person ever tested* is tests completed over people tested at least
once. People are grouped by their state at the positive test: MCI and dementia, which
together make *any CI*, and *healthy*, people who tested positive while not yet impaired
(healthy or transitional cognitive impairment) and became impaired later in the program.
Percentages are shares of everyone detected, healthy included, so MCI, dementia and
healthy sum to 100. No ratio is given for the healthy group, since the test that flagged
them preceded the impairment, and they are left out of every ratio's denominator. Table 1
counts them differently: there a positive given before onset counts as a true positive
once the person is impaired, so its sensitivity and PPV include them. The two timing
columns, in years, are among people whose impairment began during the program, as in
Table S3: *time from onset to detection* among those detected after onset, which leaves
out people already impaired at age `r min(d$testing_window)`; *time from detection to
onset* among those flagged before onset, 1 for a positive the year before onset. BHA,
brief cognitive assessment; CI, cognitive impairment.

\newpage

# 2. Supplement: testing strategies

## Table S1. Testing uptake inputs

```{r tabS1}
tu <- as_grouped_data(d$uptake_inputs, groups = "Block")
ft(tu) |>
  set_header_labels(Measure = "") |>
  bold(i = ~ !is.na(Block)) |>
  padding(i = ~ is.na(Block), j = 1, padding.left = 14) |>
  align(j = -1, align = "right", part = "body")
```

Among people due for a test. The probability of being tested at a first offer is the
probability of being offered one times the probability of completing it. *Refused last
cycle* is the probability of completing a test at the next offer after refusing one,
whatever the cognitive status; under the reactive strategy every offer is completed, so
no one refuses. \*Both selective strategies use the same probabilities of completing a
test, set for the eRADAR strategy. They differ in who is offered one and in whether it
persists: an eRADAR flag, once raised, stays on the record, while the question is asked
anew at each visit. MCI, mild cognitive impairment.

## Table S2. Brief cognitive assessment (BHA) test performance characteristics

```{r tabS2}
ft(d$bha_params) |> width(j = 1, width = 2.4) |>
  set_table_properties(layout = "autofit", width = 0.45)
```

Source: Tsoy et al. 2021, BHA-Global Score (including the informant survey) at the -1.5z cutoff.

\newpage

## Table S3. Timing of detection and time labeled positive while unimpaired, by strategy

```{r tabS3}
tb <- as_grouped_data(d$timing_burden, groups = "Block")
ft(tb) |>
  set_header_labels(Measure = "") |>
  bold(i = ~ !is.na(Block)) |>
  padding(i = ~ is.na(Block), j = 1, padding.left = 14) |>
  align(j = -1, align = "right", part = "body")
```

The first two blocks describe people whose impairment began during the program while they
were in it (with a provider and no prior clinical diagnosis); people already impaired at
age `r min(d$testing_window)` are excluded. Each falls in exactly one outcome by age
`r max(d$testing_window)`: flagged positive before onset, detected by a positive test after
onset, diagnosed clinically before the program detected them, or not detected (including
deaths). Years from onset counts 0 for detection in the onset year. *Detected within k
years* is among people whose onset left at least k years of program to be detected in. The last
block counts everyone who held a positive result while unimpaired (healthy or transitional
cognitive impairment), from that positive to impairment, death, or age
`r max(d$testing_window)`, whichever came first; *later impaired* means impaired at any
age. IQR, interquartile range; SD, standard deviation.

\newpage

## Table S8. Program performance with perfect primary care follow-up of a positive BHA

```{r tabS8}
results_ft(d$results_pcp)
```

A positive BHA is followed up by the primary care provider (PCP), who confirms every
impaired person and dismisses every false positive; the PCP verdict replaces the BHA
result in the same cycle. People whose positive is dismissed stay in the program and
are offered testing again; testing stops at a confirmed positive. This bounds how much
confirmatory follow-up could reduce the burden of false positives. Definitions, and notes
1 and 2, as in Table 1.

`r sens_dem_note(d$results_pcp)`

## Table S9. Number needed to test with perfect primary care follow-up of a positive BHA

```{r tabS9}
nnt_ft(d$nnt_pcp)
```

Definitions as in Table 2 and Table S8. There is no *healthy at time of positive test*
block: the PCP dismisses every positive given before onset, so there are none by
construction.
